entries.name: What the suite itself costs: its wall clock and its collected count
entries.rule: one ordinary single-process `pytest -q` from the repository root finishes under 4,500 s AND collects at least the cases it collects today. The seconds are a MACHINE-decided number (kpi_rules.MACHINE_KINDS): recorded everywhere, judged only on the quiet reference machine (Apple M4, 10 cores). The collected count is nobody's machine and is judged everywhere, because seconds bought by running fewer cases is the one saving a speed landing may not make
entries.measured_on: the whole suite, one process, no shards, from the repository root -- the same single-process run the CI split divides across jobs and does not make cheaper. `cases_reported` counts the cases pytest reported passed, failed or errored, so it is the collected count less the skips, and `exit` is recorded beside them as context: what the suite COSTS is this entry's subject, and whether it is green is every other entry's and the suite's own
entries.evidence: RE-STAMPED ON THE QUIET MACHINE on 1578bee, the tree that closed stage 3: 3,963.9 s over 7,654 collected and 7,602 reported, EXIT 0, at a one-minute load average of 2.5 as it began and 1.9 as it ended. The close of stage 3's review read 3,982.8 s over 7,647 and exit 1. Against 3,085.8 over 7,109 the suite grew by 545 cases with stage 3 and the seconds with it; it stands 536 s inside its 4,500-second bound, and the five-shard wall clock is about 20 minutes. THE FIVE SHARDS OF THE SAME COMMIT report 7,601 passed and 50 skipped against this run's 7,602 and 49: ONE case skips under the split CI runs and runs here, by design: the claim inventory's check of the state page's stated count, which stands down on any selected run and which CI's shard-coverage job carries through tools/ci/shards.py --prove. MEASURED on this worktree, one process, with each run's load average recorded because the reference machine was shared with other work. BEFORE, on 89a598d: 7,087 collected in 3,809.4 s at a one-minute load average of 2.8 to 6.6, the twenty slowest 2,087.5 s of it (55 per cent) and the top three 1,323.7 s (35 per cent), two of those three fixture SETUP rather than a slow case. AFTER, on the landing 1d62d4a: 7,107 collected in 3,589.2 s under the same sharing, a second run of the same code reading 3,480.4 s. AFTER THE REPAIR PASS, on 59a8fec and on a near-quiet machine (one-minute load average 3.03 as the run began, 2.43 as it ended): 7,109 collected in 3,085.8 s (51 min 25 s), 7,059 passed, 49 skipped, 1 failed. That is the number this entry now carries, and it is the first of the three taken on a machine close to quiet: the state page records 3,282 s for the predecessor tree on a quiet machine, so the same measurement made the same way reads 196 s (6 per cent) less on this tree with 22 more cases. THE ONE FAILING CASE is the state page's own record of the collected count -- the page says 7,087 and the tree collects 7,109 -- which moves in the commit that updates that page; tools/ci/shards.py --prove reports the same two numbers. The run began at a load average of 3.03, a hair above reference_machine.quiet_load_average_below, so the seconds are RECORDED here and judged nowhere (kpi_rules.seconds_judged_here). The bound of 4,500 s is an hour and a quarter on the reference machine: a ceiling that stops the suite drifting back towards the 1 h 20 m to 3 h the two-core CI cells were reading, not a target.
